identity.title: LASER: Learning Active Sensing for Continuum Field Reconstruction

problem.claim: Reconstruct high-fidelity continuum physical fields under sparse and constrained sensing.

gap.claim: Conventional methods typically use fixed sensor layouts and cannot adapt to evolving physical states.

contributions.claim: LASER is proposed as a unified closed-loop active-sensing framework formulated as a POMDP.
It uses a continuum-field latent world model to represent physical dynamics and provide intrinsic reward feedback.
It enables reinforcement-learning policies to simulate counterfactual sensing scenarios and move toward potentially informative regions using predicted latent states.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors distinguish LASER as a unified, closed-loop POMDP formulation of active sensing built around a continuum-field latent world model.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that LASER consistently outperforms static and offline-optimized strategies in experiments.
The authors report high-fidelity reconstruction under sparse sensing across diverse continuum fields.

narrative_sequence.summary: High-fidelity continuum-field measurement is important but difficult when sensing is sparse and constrained.
Fixed sensor layouts used by conventional reconstruction methods do not adapt to changing physical states.
LASER formulates active sensing as a closed-loop POMDP using a latent world model, intrinsic rewards, and latent-space what-if simulation.
The authors report that latent-state-conditioned sensor movement reaches potentially informative regions and outperforms static and offline-optimized strategies across diverse fields.

source_observation.claim: The abstract links the proposed sensing policy to an explicit latent world model, intrinsic reward, counterfactual simulation, and predicted-state-conditioned movement.

lessons.interpretation: A method claim becomes more intelligible when its internal mechanism is connected to the decision it is intended to improve.
lessons.application: When presenting an adaptive data-collection method, map each modeling component to the sensing or reconstruction decision it informs, including the feedback path.
lessons.exception: This framing may be unsuitable when the method has no sequential decisions, latent-state model, or feedback loop.

unknowns: The abstract gives no quantitative reconstruction metrics, dataset or field details, sensing budgets, or statistical variability.
The scope and implementation of the POMDP, latent world model, intrinsic reward, and reinforcement-learning policy are unspecified.
The reported comparisons do not establish independently verified effectiveness or explain whether all strategies used matched sensing constraints.
